apps.name: PeakPad
apps.tagline: 29 tools. One notch.
apps.description:
PeakPad turns the MacBook notch into a full control center packed with 29 tools, all one hover away. Instead of digging through menus, windows and browser tabs, you hover over the notch to see what's playing, grab something from your clipboard, drop files on a shelf, start a timer or check your calendar and reminders. It also goes further than most notch apps: it can show live sales and traffic from Stripe, Polar, Dodo, Lemon Squeezy, Gumroad, Paddle, Shopify and Google Analytics, track your Claude Code and Codex token usage, and answer questions with Apple's on-device AI through Ask Peak, so nothing you type leaves your Mac. It runs on Apple silicon and Intel Macs with macOS Sonoma or later.

Key Features:

- Notch Control Center: now playing, calendar, reminders, app shortcuts, volume and brightness in one panel

- Ask Peak: private, on-device AI answers powered by Apple's models, right in the notch

- Revenue & Analytics: see sales from Stripe, Gumroad, Paddle, Shopify and more, plus Google Analytics traffic

- AI Usage Tracking: tokens, messages and streaks from Claude Code and Codex, read from local logs

- Productivity Tools: clipboard history, file shelf, timers, teleprompter and more, 29 tools in total

PeakPad is a one-time-purchase notch app that brings 29 tools, from media controls to revenue dashboards and private AI, into a single glance at the top of your Mac.

apps.name: Trailback
apps.tagline: Can't find it? Just describe it.
apps.description:
Trailback finds the file, web page or screenshot you lost, even when you've forgotten its name, where you saved it or which browser it was in. It quietly remembers what you open and see on your computer, so describing what you remember is enough. Ask for "that hotel with the pool" and it brings back the page you closed days ago, the screenshot of the price table and the PDF booking confirmation, all grouped by what you were working on. It reads the words inside screenshots and documents, tracks which website each download came from, and understands what you mean rather than just matching exact words. It works 100% offline, never records private windows, and runs on Mac and Windows.

Key Features:

- Find Closed Pages: bring back any page you visited, even after clearing your history, in any browser

- Screenshot Search: find screenshots by any word that appears inside them

- Document Search: locate PDFs, Word files and notes by what's inside them

- Download Origins: see which website every download came from

- Fully Offline: nothing leaves your computer and private windows are never recorded

Trailback is an offline, describe-it-to-find-it search tool that recovers lost pages, screenshots and files, available for a one-time $5 launch price (normally $29).

apps.name: Pungo
apps.tagline: Custom cursors. Clearer presentations.
apps.description:
Pungo is a Mac app that adds personality to the things you do a hundred times a day. It gives you original custom cursor packs that you can browse, preview and apply in seconds, choosing your size and keeping only the cursors you love while the rest stay at the macOS default. For presentations, Pungo lets you point, draw and zoom over any Mac app with a floating toolbar, freehand drawing, arrows, shapes, numbered steps and spotlight effects, all switchable with keyboard shortcuts. It also includes Keep Awake, which stops your Mac sleeping on a timer or until your AI task finishes, and a helper that restores your cursor after a restart.

Key Features:

- Custom Cursor Packs: original pointer, link and grab cursors you can preview and apply instantly

- Pick and Choose: change only the cursors you like and keep the macOS defaults for the rest

- Presentation Tools: point, draw, zoom and highlight over any app with a floating toolbar

- Annotations: freehand drawing, arrows, shapes and numbered steps with keyboard shortcuts

- Keep Awake: keep your Mac awake on a timer or until an AI task finishes

Pungo combines playful custom cursors, on-screen presentation tools and Keep Awake in one Mac app for a single €7.99 license.

apps.name: Lounge
apps.tagline: Your menu bar, perfectly organized.
apps.description:
Lounge is a menu bar manager for macOS and a modern, notch-aware alternative to Bartender. Every app wants a spot in your menu bar, and on MacBooks the notch can hide the icons you need most. Lounge lets you hide and reveal menu bar items so your bar stays clean, and you can drag icons between sections by holding Command and dragging them across the divider. Hover near the notch to open a panel that shows all your hidden and displayed icons in clear sections, with clipboard history built in. A single settings panel covers launch at login, the Lounge icon, keyboard shortcuts and licensing. It requires macOS 26 Tahoe or later.

Key Features:

- Hide and Reveal: keep the menu bar clean by tucking away icons you rarely use

- Drag and Drop: hold Command and drag icons across the divider to rearrange them

- Notch-Aware Panel: hover near the notch to see every hidden and visible icon

- Built-in Clipboard History: search, review and reuse recent copies from the notch panel

- Keyboard Shortcuts: toggle hidden items instantly and configure everything from one settings panel

Lounge is a lightweight, notch-friendly menu bar organizer for macOS Tahoe, priced at $3.99 per year after a 7-day free trial.

apps.name: RollFerry
apps.tagline: Get your photos off your phone and onto your Mac.
apps.description:
RollFerry is a Mac app that copies photos and videos off an Android phone over USB, filling the gap left by the discontinued Android File Transfer. Plug in your phone and RollFerry reads what's on it in seconds, showing only the photos and videos that aren't on your Mac yet, grouped by month. Pick a month, a range or everything and it crosses each file over, checking every copy byte for byte with SHA-256. If you unplug halfway it picks up where it stopped, and it only offers to free space on your phone for files it has verified on your Mac. It never uploads anything, needs no account, works offline and runs in Apple's sandbox.

Key Features:

- Only What's New: see photos and videos not yet on your Mac, organized by month

- Verified Copies: every file is checked with SHA-256 before it counts as transferred

- Resumable Transfers: unplug mid-way and it continues exactly where it stopped

- Safe Space Freeing: deletes from the phone only files proven to be on your Mac, and only when you ask

- Fully Private: no uploads, no account, works offline and runs in Apple's sandbox

RollFerry is a simple, verified way to move photos and videos from an Android phone to a Mac, sold as a one-time purchase with a free trial.

apps.name: Sorted
apps.tagline: Drop files. Sorted does the rest.
apps.description:
Sorted is an AI file organizer that turns scattered files into a private local library that keeps organizing itself. It watches folders like Downloads for new arrivals, extracts content from PDFs, scans, images and Office documents, adds useful tags and proposes a clear destination only when a separate folder actually helps. It finds exact and visual duplicates, applies custom rules that always win, and lets you search by meaning rather than filename. You can ask follow-up questions about your documents and get answers with citations to the exact page, and at tax time export a reviewable Tax Pack with the source documents your accountant needs. All of it runs locally on your Mac.

Key Features:

- Watched Folders: new files are read, tagged and routed automatically as they arrive

- Duplicate Review: find exact and visually similar duplicates and clean them up safely

- Meaning-Based Search: find documents by what they contain, not what they were named

- Cited Answers: ask questions about your files and open the cited page to verify

- Custom Rules and Tax Pack: route and tag files your way and export organized tax records

Sorted is a local, AI-powered file organizer for Mac that tidies, deduplicates and lets you search and question your documents for a one-time $9.99.

apps.name: Hushmark
apps.tagline: Redact before AI. Keep private data out.
apps.description:
Hushmark is a privacy gate for your AI workflow. Before you paste a document into an LLM or share it elsewhere, Hushmark finds and removes names, addresses, phone numbers, account numbers and other sensitive information from PDFs, Word documents, CSVs, text, HTML and images. Everything runs locally: no uploads, no accounts and no copies stored. Detection happens on your device, you review and adjust every match using templates and field groups, then export a secure copy with permanent redactions. The browser version is free to use, and the Mac app adds custom templates and batch redaction for a one-time purchase.

Key Features:

- Local Detection: sensitive fields are identified privately on your device, nothing is uploaded

- Review and Customize: pick a template, adjust field groups and inspect every match before exporting

- Permanent Redactions: export a secure copy that is safe to share with AI tools

- Wide Format Support: PDF, DOCX, CSV, TXT, HTML, PNG, JPG and WEBP

- Mac App Extras: custom reusable templates and batch redaction into a secure export folder

Hushmark strips personal data from your documents locally before they reach an AI tool, free in the browser with a $4.99 Mac app for power users.

apps.name: Markdific
apps.tagline: Markdown Viewer and Editor for Mac, Windows and Linux
apps.description:
Markdific is a Markdown viewer and editor for opening, editing and exporting .md files. You can edit visually in WYSIWYG mode with no Markdown syntax in the way, or work with the raw source and see a live preview beside it in split view. It renders everything properly, including Mermaid diagrams, tables, code, task lists, alerts, charts, front matter, images, LaTeX math and footnotes. Themes and fonts make long reading comfortable, and finished documents can be exported to PDF, Word or self-contained HTML with their diagrams and tables included. On the Mac it also adds Quick Look support, so you can press Space on a .md file in Finder to see it formatted.

Key Features:

- Three Editing Modes: WYSIWYG live editor, Markdown source and split view with live preview

- Full Rendering: Mermaid diagrams, tables, code, task lists, alerts, charts, math and front matter

- Export Anywhere: PDF (Letter, A4 or Legal), editable Word .docx, HTML or Markdown

- Themes and Fonts: Original, Dark, Creammy, Solarized and High Contrast with a choice of typefaces

- Quick Look and Tabs: preview .md files from Finder and keep several documents open with an outline

Markdific is a polished Markdown reader and editor that renders, edits and exports .md files for a one-time price, with a 14-day free trial.

apps.name: Fling
apps.tagline: Instant Command Wheel for your Mac.
apps.description:
Fling is a macOS application that adds a radial command wheel at your cursor. Hold a shortcut, flick toward an action and release to launch apps, open links, snap windows or run shortcuts. This tool is designed for power users, designers, and developers who want their most-used actions at their fingertips.

Key Features:

- Opens a 15-slot command wheel at your cursor with a held shortcut.

- Launches apps, folders, URLs and deep links with a single flick.

- Snaps windows left, right or maximized instantly.

- Samples any screen pixel and copies HEX, RGB or HSL values.

- Triggers keyboard shortcuts and system actions visually, using little CPU and memory.

Fling is a macOS command wheel that puts your 15 most-used apps and actions at your cursor. Hold, flick and release to launch, snap windows or pick colors.

apps.name: NotchMomo
apps.tagline: A little friend. A happier Mac.
apps.description:
Momo is a macOS application that adds an animated companion to your MacBook notch, along with everyday productivity tools. It includes a focus timer, notes, clipboard history, a file shelf and quick links, all one hover away. This tool is designed for Mac users who want a friendly, playful notch app that also helps them focus and stay organized.

Key Features:

- Adds an animated notch companion with four looks, six colours and twelve expressions.

- Runs Pomodoro sessions, countdowns and a stopwatch with stretch and water reminders.

- Keeps named notes with search, pinning and local autosave.

- Includes a file shelf with an image converter and clipboard history.

- Works on Macs without a notch and keeps notes and clips on your Mac.

Momo is a macOS notch app with an animated companion and handy tools like a focus timer, notes, clipboard history and a file shelf. It makes your Mac feel friendlier while keeping everyday tools close.

apps.name: Maclip
apps.tagline: Never lose anything you copy on macOS.
apps.description:
Maclip is a macOS application that functions as a clipboard manager that opens right at your text cursor. It saves everything you copy, encrypted on your Mac, and adds paste stacks, snippets, per-app rules and a private MCP server for AI apps. This tool is designed for developers, writers, and professionals who copy and paste all day and want a fast, private clipboard.

Key Features:

- Opens your clipboard history at the text cursor with Command-Shift-V.

- Queues several clips and pastes them in order to fill forms quickly.

- Pastes plain text anywhere, with per-app formatting rules.

- Lets Claude, Cursor and other AI apps search clips only after you approve.

- Encrypts history on your Mac, locks boards with Touch ID and auto-erases 2FA codes.

Maclip is a macOS clipboard manager that opens at your cursor and keeps every clip encrypted on your Mac. It adds paste stacks, snippets and AI access you approve, for a one-time price.

apps.name: StitchSlide
apps.tagline: One canvas. Every swipe.
apps.description:
StitchSlide is a carousel maker for Instagram, LinkedIn and TikTok that lets you design on one wide canvas and splits it into seamless slides. Photos, text and drawings can sit across slide edges so each swipe flows into the next. This tool is designed for creators, marketers, and small brands who want eye-catching carousels without complex design software.

Key Features:

- Designs the whole carousel on one canvas and cuts it into perfect slides.

- Lets photos and text span across slide edges for seamless swipes.

- Includes 16 photo layouts, 69 fonts and support for custom fonts.

- Supports drawing with a stylus and a brand kit for colors and logos.

- Exports slides as PNG, MP4 or PDF, with no account required.

StitchSlide is a free carousel maker that turns one wide canvas into seamless, swipeable slides for Instagram, LinkedIn and TikTok. It runs in your browser with no sign-up.

apps.name: GlidePage
apps.tagline: Any website. One smooth scrolling video.
apps.description:
GlidePage is a macOS application that records any website as a smooth 4K, 60 fps scrolling video inside a real device frame. Paste a link, pick a device and record, and GlidePage captures every frame for a perfectly smooth result. This tool is designed for founders, designers, and marketers who need polished website videos for launches and portfolios.

Key Features:

- Records any website, including localhost and staging sites, as a scrolling video.

- Exports in 4K at 60 fps, plus stills and transparent clips.

- Frames recordings in real iPhone, Pixel, iPad, MacBook and iMac devices.

- Offers six easing curves, adjustable speed and pauses.

- Captures live pages with animations and sticky headers, all on your Mac.

GlidePage is a macOS app that turns any website into a smooth 4K, 60 fps scrolling video in a real device frame. Paste a link, pick a device and record, with no editing needed.

apps.name: Plumby
apps.tagline: Your Mac is full. But of what?
apps.description:
Plumby is a macOS application that finds the caches, logs, old device backups and installers filling up your Mac. It explains each item in a plain sentence and only removes what you choose, with your personal files left unticked by default. This tool is designed for Mac users who are running out of storage and want a cleaner they can trust.

Key Features:

- Shows what is using your disk space, from apps and photos to clutter.

- Finds caches, temporary files, logs, iPhone backups and old installers.

- Explains each item, what happens if it goes, and whether it grows back.

- Removes app leftovers like caches, preferences and helpers when you delete an app.

- Keeps your files on your Mac and sends personal files to the Trash, not straight to deletion.

Plumby is a macOS cleaner that shows where your disk space went and explains everything it can remove before you decide. It clears caches, backups and app leftovers while keeping your own files safe.

apps.name: Precis
apps.tagline: Talk. It types.
apps.description:
Precis is a macOS application for private voice dictation that types clean text in any app. Hold Option-Space, speak, and Precis removes filler words, applies corrections and shapes the text for the app you are using, with speech recognition running on your Mac. This tool is designed for professionals, writers, and developers who want fast dictation without sending their voice to the cloud.

Key Features:

- Types dictated text at your cursor in any app with a hold-to-talk shortcut.

- Removes filler words and applies spoken corrections like "no wait".

- Shapes text into the right style for emails, messages, notes or AI prompts.

- Runs speech recognition and styles fully on your Mac, with no audio sent anywhere.

- Supports 99 languages and shows a small capsule beside your cursor while listening.

Precis is a macOS dictation app that turns your speech into clean, app-appropriate text right at your cursor. Everything runs on your Mac, with no account and no subscription.

apps.name: NotchDodo
apps.tagline: The Dynamic Island for your MacBook.
apps.description:
NotchDodo is a macOS application that turns the MacBook notch into a Dynamic Island with 18 tools. It brings music, timers, today's calendar, files, notes and AI agent usage into a panel one hover above the menu bar. This tool is designed for developers, makers, and productivity-focused Mac users who want their day organized at the top of the screen.

Key Features:

- Shows a dashboard with calendar, tasks, notes, reminders and quick toggles.

- Runs Pomodoro sessions with focus sounds and a countdown in the notch.

- Tracks Claude Code usage and lists running local dev servers.

- Includes clipboard history, a file shelf, music controls and a calculator.

- Works on Macs without a notch and keeps everything on your Mac.

NotchDodo is a macOS application that turns the notch into a Dynamic Island with 18 tools, from a daily dashboard to Pomodoro timers and AI usage tracking. It keeps your day one hover away for a one-time price.

apps.name: Orcylo
apps.tagline: Slow Mac? Claude limit? New sale? Know at a glance.
apps.description:
Orcylo is a macOS application that works as an Activity Monitor alternative in your menu bar. It groups hundreds of processes into the apps you recognize, keeps 30 days of history, and also shows AI coding limits and today's sales. This tool is designed for developers, founders, and power users who want to understand their Mac's performance at a glance.

Key Features:

- Groups about 700 processes into roughly 25 recognizable apps.

- Shows CPU, memory, GPU, disk, network and power as customizable menu bar readouts.

- Keeps 30 days of local history to see what slowed your Mac down.

- Tracks Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Gemini CLI limits with reset countdowns.

- Displays today's sales and site visitors alongside system stats.

Orcylo is a macOS menu bar app that replaces Activity Monitor with a clear, app-level view of CPU, memory, power and more. It also tracks AI coding limits and today's sales, with 30 days of local history.

apps.name: SearchOnMac
apps.tagline: Find anything on your Mac. Just describe it.
apps.description:
SearchOnMac is a macOS application that lets you search your Mac by describing what you remember. It finds files, apps, windows, browser tabs, mail, calendar events and clipboard history using local AI, without needing exact file names. This tool is designed for professionals and power users who struggle to find files with Spotlight.

Key Features:

- Searches by meaning, so phrases like "the pdf I downloaded this morning" find the right file.

- Finds documents, photos, apps, windows, tabs, Mail, Calendar and clipboard items in one search.

- Previews files and offers actions like open, reveal in Finder, copy path and share.

- Opens from anywhere with Option-Space and returns results in about a tenth of a second.

- Keeps all searches and AI ranking on your Mac.

SearchOnMac is a macOS search launcher that finds files, apps, windows and clipboard items from a plain description of what you remember. It uses local AI, so searches never leave your Mac.

apps.name: MacFold
apps.tagline: Close the lid. Watch your desktop bend.
apps.description:
MacFold is a macOS application that adds a folding animation to your MacBook as you close the lid. It reads the hinge angle and makes your desktop tilt, blur and settle like a foldable phone, all processed on your Mac. This tool is designed for MacBook owners who enjoy visual polish and fun desktop effects.

Key Features:

- Tilts, blurs and dims your live desktop as you lower the lid.

- Reads the MacBook's lid-angle sensor in real time.

- Renders windows, wallpaper and cursor together with ScreenCaptureKit and Metal.

- Lives in the menu bar, where you can pause or adjust the effect.

- Processes frames in memory on your Mac and never writes them to disk.

MacFold is a macOS application that makes your desktop tilt and blur as you close your MacBook's lid, like a foldable phone. It uses the hinge sensor and runs entirely on your Mac.

apps.name: Here
apps.tagline: Clipboard at cursor, without keyboard.
apps.description:
Here is a macOS application that brings your clipboard history to your cursor. Double right-click anywhere to open a small clipboard panel, then click an item to paste it, so your hand never has to leave the mouse. This tool is designed for designers, researchers, and anyone who works mouse-first and wants faster copy and paste.

Key Features:

- Opens clipboard history at your cursor with a double right-click.

- Pastes text, links and images with a single click.

- Shows a side hover preview before you paste.

- Filters clips by text, links or images.

- Works fully offline with no cloud, account or internet connection.

Here is a macOS clipboard extension that opens your clipboard history right at your cursor with a double right-click. It lets you paste text, links and images without touching the keyboard.

apps.name: Assist
apps.tagline: One notch. Everyday tools.
apps.description:
Assist is a macOS application that brings clipboard history, a file shelf, quick notes, focus timers and other modules into the MacBook notch. It also captures and annotates screenshots, including voice annotations transcribed on your Mac. This tool is designed for developers, founders, and productivity-focused Mac users who want everyday tools close at hand.

Key Features:

- Keeps clipboard history, a file shelf and a quick notes scratchpad in the notch.

- Runs Pomodoro, countdown and stopwatch timers with hydration reminders.

- Shows calendar events, reminders, music controls, system stats and screen time.

- Tracks revenue from Stripe, Polar or Dodo and Claude Code and Codex activity.

- Captures screenshots with quick edits and voice annotations transcribed locally.

Assist is a macOS application that packs clipboard history, a file shelf, notes, focus timers and other modules into the notch. It also captures screenshots with voice annotations, all for a one-time price.

apps.name: NotchMind
apps.tagline: Small notch. Big mind.
apps.description:
NotchMind is a macOS application that turns the MacBook notch into a home for music, files, clipboard history, timers and 28 everyday tools. It opens with a hover and shows what you need in the one spot your eyes already go. This tool is designed for Mac users and creators who want quick access to media controls and everyday utilities without switching apps.

Key Features:

- Controls music, switches speakers and shows what's playing from the notch.

- Holds dragged files in a tray and sends them via AirDrop.

- Shows download progress and converts files to PNG, JPEG, HEIC, PDF or ZIP in place.

- Offers timers, natural-language reminders and weather at a glance.

- Includes a smart clipboard that recognizes colors, JSON and links and clears copied secrets.

NotchMind is a macOS application that turns the notch into a hub for music, files, clipboard history, timers and everyday tools. It keeps 28 utilities one hover away with a one-time purchase.

apps.name: Cuewake
apps.tagline: Leave it here. Find it when you're back.
apps.description:
Cuewake is a macOS application for leaving notes, checklists, links and files as cues to pick up later. It saves the context of what you were working on, such as the app, page or file, and helps you return to the right place when you come back. This tool is designed for busy professionals, makers, and students who juggle many tasks and want to resume work without losing their thread.

Key Features:

- Captures notes, checklists, links and files as cues from any app.

- Saves the app, window, page or file context so you can return to it.

- Organizes cues into Waiting, Later and Done, with search and filters by type.

- Works fully offline with no account or cloud.

- Uses a one-time license with lifetime updates.

Cuewake is a macOS application that lets you leave notes, checklists, links and files as cues and find them waiting when you come back. It saves your working context so you can pick up exactly where you left off.

apps.name: DejaShot
apps.tagline: You screenshotted it. DejaShot finds it.
apps.description:
DejaShot is a macOS application that makes your screenshots searchable by the text inside them. It reads every screenshot in your chosen folders and records which app each new one came from, so you can find it by what you remember, all on your Mac. This tool is designed for designers, developers, and professionals who take screenshots instead of notes and struggle to find them later.

Key Features:

- Reads the text inside every screenshot in the folders you choose.

- Records the app and window title for each new screenshot.

- Opens a search panel from anywhere with Shift-Command-Space.

- Supports filters like app:figma, after:march, exact phrases and has:text.

- Processes everything locally and pauses indexing to save battery.

DejaShot is a macOS application that reads the text in your screenshots and remembers which app they came from. It lets you find any screenshot by typing what you remember, all processed privately on your Mac.

apps.name: StepAway
apps.tagline: Stop Eye Strain. Protect Your Rest. Reclaim Your Flow.
apps.description:
StepAway is a macOS application that functions as a meeting-aware break timer for eye strain relief and better posture. It lives in the menu bar, reminds you to rest your eyes, blink and straighten up, and pauses automatically when you step away or join a call. This tool is designed for developers, designers, and anyone who spends long hours at a Mac and wants healthier work habits.

Key Features:

- Reminds you to take 20-20-20 eye breaks from a native menu bar timer.

- Nudges you to fix your posture with a Spine Align drop-down HUD.

- Adds gentle blink reminders to help prevent dry eyes.

- Pauses timers when you leave your desk and postpones breaks during Zoom or Slack calls.

- Includes guided eye and stretch exercises and a GitHub-style activity heatmap.

StepAway is a macOS break timer that reminds you to rest your eyes, blink and fix your posture. It pauses automatically during meetings and when you step away, so breaks never interrupt real work.

apps.name: StowLink
apps.tagline: Your links, neatly stowed.
apps.description:
StowLink is a macOS application that functions as a native bookmark manager. It lets you save, organize and search links with rich previews, nested folders and notes, and syncs with a free iPhone app. This tool is designed for developers, designers, and researchers who save lots of links and want them out of a cluttered bookmark bar.

Key Features:

- Imports bookmarks from Safari, Chrome, Firefox and Edge.

- Saves links from anywhere with a global shortcut, without opening the app.

- Organizes links in nested folders with rich previews, notes and playable videos.

- Searches by title, URL, domain or description, with a Command-K spotlight.

- Keeps your library local, with optional iCloud sync to the free iPhone app.

StowLink is a native macOS bookmark manager that saves, organizes and searches your links with rich previews and nested folders. It imports from all major browsers and syncs with a free iPhone app.

apps.name: MacDelta
apps.tagline: Change Log for Your Mac.
apps.description:
MacDelta is a macOS application that records what changes on your Mac in a local timeline. It tracks app installs and updates, growing folders, background items, network and Bluetooth connections, battery events and more. This tool is designed for power users, developers, and IT-minded Mac owners who want to understand what changed on their system and when.

Key Features:

- Records app installs, updates and removals with version numbers.

- Tracks folder size changes, such as Downloads or Developer growing.

- Logs new, changed or removed background items like LaunchAgents and LaunchDaemons.

- Records Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, drive, display, battery, sleep and thermal events.

- Saves snapshots for comparison and exports your change history, all stored locally.

MacDelta is a macOS application that keeps a local timeline of everything that changes on your Mac, from app updates and background items to folder sizes and connections. It helps you see exactly what changed and when.

apps.name: Helumi
apps.tagline: More space for your Mac, without buying a new one.
apps.description:
Helumi is a macOS application that adds a cloud drive to Finder with terabytes of space and zero bytes used on your Mac. Files look and open like normal, but they live in the cloud and stream only the parts you need, so large videos start playing instantly. This tool is designed for video editors, photographers, and creators who work with large files and are running out of disk space.

Key Features:

- Adds a Helumi drive in Finder, next to Macintosh HD, with up to 30 TB of space.

- Streams only the part of a file you need, so large videos start in under a second.

- Keeps files off your disk, with an option to keep folders offline.

- Shares files with a link and collects files from anyone.

- Restores deleted files for 30 days and resumes interrupted uploads.

Helumi is a macOS application that gives your Mac terabytes of cloud storage as a normal Finder drive, using zero local disk space. Files stream on demand, so even huge videos open instantly.

apps.name: Droppy
apps.tagline: Supercharged Dynamic Island for your Mac.
apps.description:
Droppy is a macOS application that turns the notch into a Dynamic Island with live activities, a file tray, clipboard history and over 30 extensions. It replaces a dock full of utilities with one app and works on Macs with or without a notch. This tool is designed for Mac users, creators, and developers who want media controls and everyday tools right at the top of their screen.

Key Features:

- Shows live activities for music, meetings, uploads and volume around the notch.

- Includes a file tray that can zip or convert files, plus clipboard history.

- Offers a floating music player with queue, lyrics and lock screen controls.

- Lets you reply to iMessage, WhatsApp and Telegram and control Zoom, Teams and Meet from the notch.

- Adds 39 free extensions, screen recording, per-app volume and Pomodoro timers.

Droppy is a macOS application that turns the notch into a supercharged Dynamic Island with live activities, a file tray, clipboard history and dozens of extensions. It brings music, messages and everyday tools to the top of your screen for a one-time price.

apps.name: ClearBar
apps.tagline: A clean menu bar. Without losing a single app.
apps.description:
ClearBar is a macOS application that hides menu bar icons while keeping every app one click away. It gathers hidden apps, including ones lost behind the notch, into a single panel that shows each app's memory use and lets you quit it. This tool is designed for Mac users with crowded menu bars who want a cleaner, lighter alternative to Bartender and Ice.

Key Features:

- Hides third-party menu bar icons in one click, leaving Apple's system items in place.

- Keeps every hidden app in one panel, where clicking a tile opens its menu.

- Shows memory use for each app, with heavy apps highlighted.

- Quits or force quits apps directly from the panel.

- Needs only Accessibility permission, never Screen Recording.

ClearBar is a macOS menu bar manager that hides cluttered icons and keeps every app reachable from one panel. It also shows each app's memory use and lets you quit memory-heavy apps in a click.

apps.name: Drain
apps.tagline: Track what's running low, before it runs out.
apps.description:
Drain is a macOS application that shows everything running low on your MacBook as a thin line around the notch. It tracks battery, memory, storage, data and AI coding limits, and explains which apps and processes are using each resource. This tool is designed for MacBook users and developers who want to see what is draining their resources before it runs out.

Key Features:

- Displays battery, memory, storage, data and AI limits as a line around the notch.

- Shows which apps, projects and processes use battery, memory and data.

- Tracks Claude Code and Codex usage limits and reset times.

- Shows Wi-Fi signal, live network speed and hotspot data usage.

- Works in the menu bar on Macs without a notch.

Drain is a macOS application that shows battery, memory, storage, data and AI coding limits as a thin line around the notch. It explains what is using each resource so you can act before it runs out.

apps.name: Voicera
apps.tagline: Don't type. Just speak.
apps.description:
Voicera is a macOS application that turns natural speech into clean, polished writing. It types directly into any app, removes filler words and adds punctuation, and offers AI actions to rewrite, fix, translate or answer questions. This tool is designed for professionals, writers, and anyone who wants to write faster by speaking instead of typing.

Key Features:

- Converts speech to polished text about 4× faster than typing, directly at your cursor.

- Removes filler words, handles corrections and adds punctuation automatically.

- Supports 19 languages, with switching between them mid-sentence.

- Rewrites, fixes, shortens or translates selected text with one shortcut.

- Answers questions out loud with Fn + Space, and supports custom writing styles.

Voicera is a macOS voice dictation app that turns speech into clean, ready-to-send writing in any app. It adds AI actions to rewrite, translate and answer questions, all triggered from the Fn key.

apps.name: OmniNotch
apps.tagline: It's all in the notch.
apps.description:
OmniNotch is a macOS application that adds twenty tools to the MacBook notch. It brings an on-device AI assistant, media controls, clipboard history, a file shelf, revenue tracking and everyday utilities into one lightweight panel. This tool is designed for productivity-focused Mac users, founders, and creators who want quick access to common tools without opening extra apps.

Key Features:

- Includes Ask Omni, a private AI assistant powered by Apple's on-device models.

- Shows AI usage limits for Claude, Codex, Cursor, Copilot and Grok.

- Tracks today's revenue from Stripe, Shopify, Lemon Squeezy, Gumroad, Dodo, Polar and Paddle.

- Offers clipboard history, a file shelf with AirDrop, a teleprompter, timers and a camera mirror.

- Adds calendar, reminders, to-dos, weather, stocks, emoji, unit converter, system stats and quick notes.

OmniNotch is a macOS application that packs twenty tools into the notch, from an on-device AI assistant to clipboard history, revenue tracking and a file shelf. It keeps everyday utilities one glance away with a one-time license.

apps.name: CTA
apps.tagline: A teleprompter under your notch.
apps.description:
CTA is a macOS application that functions as a teleprompter placed directly under the MacBook notch. It follows your voice as you read, scrolls your script automatically, and uses AI to help you write and polish it, while staying hidden from screen shares and recordings. This tool is designed for creators, presenters, and professionals who record videos or join calls and want to keep their eyes near the camera.

Key Features:

- Shows your script in a small panel under the notch, right below the camera.

- Follows your voice to highlight and scroll the current word, with speech recognized on your Mac.

- Stays hidden from Zoom, Meet, OBS and QuickTime during screen sharing and recording.

- Writes scripts from notes, Notion pages, Google Docs or files with AI.

- Rewrites scripts to be easier to say, fit a time limit, or follow your instructions.

CTA is a macOS teleprompter that sits under the notch and follows your voice as you read. It stays invisible on screen share and uses AI to write and polish your scripts.

apps.name: Vinaa
apps.tagline: All your AI chats in one Mac app.
apps.description:
Vinaa is a macOS application that functions as a native AI chat client for cloud and local models. It brings OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, Ollama, LM Studio and more into one app with your own API keys, keeping chat history stored on your Mac. This tool is designed for developers, writers, and professionals who use multiple AI models and want their conversations organized in one place.

Key Features:

- Supports OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Mistral, xAI, DeepSeek, Ollama and LM Studio with your own keys.

- Organizes chats into projects, folders and nested folders, with automatic filing.

- Opens multiple projects in separate windows and chats in tabs.

- Includes a prompt library with variables and MCP tool connections.

- Imports ChatGPT and Claude history and stores chats locally, with optional iCloud sync.

Vinaa is a native macOS AI chat app that brings cloud and local models together with your own API keys. It keeps conversations organized in projects and stored locally, with prompt templates, tools and chat imports.

apps.name: Drop Notch
apps.tagline: Your agents. Now in your notch.
apps.description:
Drop Notch is a macOS application that brings AI coding agents like Claude Code and Codex into the MacBook notch. It shows live tool calls, lets you approve actions, and follows sessions started in your terminals, so you can manage agents without switching windows. This tool is designed for developers who run AI coding agents and want to monitor them while they keep working.

Key Features:

- Supports 16 coding agents, including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot and Grok.

- Shows each tool call live and lets you approve or deny edits from the notch.

- Follows sessions started in terminals and lets you reply in place.

- Tracks token usage and cost by day, model and project.

- Includes music controls, a file tray, AirDrop, timers and system stats.

Drop Notch is a macOS application that puts Claude Code, Codex and 14 other coding agents in your MacBook notch. It lets you watch tool calls, approve actions and reply to agents without leaving what you are working on.

apps.name: Shotbase
apps.tagline: Capture, edit, organize, and share in one place.
apps.description:
Shotbase is a macOS application that functions as a screen capture workspace for screenshots, recordings and web pages. It combines capture, editing, AI-powered organization and sharing in one app, with AI that runs locally on your Mac. This tool is designed for designers, product teams, and creators who capture and share their screen often and want polished results without juggling multiple tools.

Key Features:

- Captures screenshots, screen recordings and full web pages at any breakpoint.

- Adds automatic zooms, 3D effects, backgrounds, frames and annotations in one editor.

- Names, tags and summarizes captures automatically using on-device AI.

- Keeps all captures in one searchable library.

- Creates share links and collects reactions and feedback in the app.

Shotbase is a macOS screen capture workspace for screenshots, recordings and web pages, with a built-in editor for annotations, zooms and 3D effects. It organizes captures with private on-device AI and makes sharing simple.

apps.name: InsurStaq AI
apps.tagline: See your code the way an attacker does.
apps.description:
InsurStaq AI is a macOS application that acts as a private AI security engineer for your codebase. It runs entirely on your Mac, traces real attack paths through your code, suggests fixes, and maps evidence to compliance frameworks. This tool is designed for developers, startups, and security teams who need security reviews without sending source code to the cloud.

Key Features:

- Traces attack paths from user input to dangerous code, not just file and line numbers.

- Explains each finding in plain English and suggests a patch to review.

- Rescans changed files to confirm a fix closes the vulnerability.

- Maps evidence to SOC 2, OWASP ASVS, PCI DSS and ISO 27001.

- Runs locally with 279 built-in rules and an offline vulnerability database.

InsurStaq AI is a macOS application that scans your codebase locally to find real attack paths, suggest fixes and verify them. It also maps findings to compliance standards, without your source code leaving your Mac.

apps.name: DockUI
apps.tagline: SwiftUI Templates & Visual Design Tools
apps.description:
DockUI is a macOS application for visually designing SwiftUI interfaces and exporting production-ready code. It combines a visual editor, a library of templates and components, and an AI design assistant. This tool is designed for iOS and macOS developers who want to prototype and build SwiftUI interfaces faster.

Key Features:

- Lets you add, resize and customize SwiftUI components visually.

- Generates clean SwiftUI code that pastes directly into Xcode.

- Includes a curated library of templates and components, updated weekly.

- Provides access to over 5,000 SF Symbols.

- Offers an AI assistant that generates and refines UI from prompts.

DockUI is a macOS application for visually designing SwiftUI interfaces and exporting ready-to-use code for Xcode. It includes templates, SF Symbols and an AI design assistant to speed up app development.

apps.name: EveryPaste
apps.tagline: One clipboard. However you work.
apps.description:
EveryPaste is a macOS application that functions as a private clipboard history manager. It saves everything you copy and brings it back instantly with Shift-Command-V, with all data kept on your Mac. This tool is designed for professionals, developers, and designers who copy and paste throughout the day and lose track of what they copied.

Key Features:

- Saves your full clipboard history, searchable by keyword, app or type.

- Reads text inside screenshots so images are searchable.

- Pastes copied items in sequence to fill forms quickly.

- Offers snippets with fill-in blanks and pinned boards for frequent items.

- Cleans links of trackers, strips formatting and converts colour formats as you paste.

EveryPaste is a macOS clipboard manager that saves everything you copy and brings it back with one shortcut. It adds searchable screenshot text, snippets, pinned boards and format cleanup, all stored privately on your Mac.

apps.name: Pastely
apps.tagline: Paste anything, exactly right.
apps.description:
Pastely is a macOS application that functions as an AI-powered smart clipboard. It reads what you copied and the app you are pasting into, then converts the content into the right format with a single hotkey. This tool is designed for professionals, developers, and anyone who regularly moves content between apps and spends time reformatting it.

Key Features:

- Formats pasted content based on the destination app and field.

- Turns messy tables, CSV or JSON into clean columns in Google Sheets.

- Rewrites emails or docs as natural chat messages for WhatsApp, iMessage or Slack.

- Fills entire online forms from a CV or saved details.

- Translates, rewrites or summarizes when you type an instruction before pasting.

Pastely is a macOS menu bar app that uses AI to convert copied content into the format the destination app needs. One hotkey turns data into spreadsheet columns, text into chat messages, or details into filled forms.

apps.name: ASO Engine
apps.tagline: Get more downloads. Rank higher.
apps.description:
ASO Engine is a macOS application for App Store keyword research and rank tracking. It helps developers find keywords worth targeting, analyze competing apps, and track rankings across countries in one workspace. This tool is designed for indie developers, app marketers, and studios who want to improve their App Store visibility.

Key Features:

- Researches App Store keywords with estimated popularity and difficulty.

- Highlights keyword opportunities based on your current rank.

- Explores competitor listings, visible keyword rankings and similar apps.

- Tracks keyword rankings over time and across countries.

- Requires no App Store account connection or sign-up.

ASO Engine is a macOS application for App Store keyword research, competitor analysis and rank tracking. It helps developers find better keywords and monitor their rankings across countries.

apps.name: Locul
apps.tagline: The second brain for your AI.
apps.description:
Locul is a macOS application that turns your notes, docs and dictations into a memory your AI tools can use. It indexes your existing content locally and keeps it up to date automatically as your decisions change. This tool is designed for founders and solo operators who rely on AI tools daily and want them to know their product, customers and decisions.

Key Features:

- Builds a memory from local files, Notion, Obsidian, dictations and LinkedIn posts.

- Updates outdated memories automatically and keeps a history of what changed.

- Creates entities for people, products, services and projects.

- Makes your memory available to Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and Codex.

- Runs locally, with an optional cloud AI mode that uses your own key.

Locul is a macOS application that turns your existing notes, docs and dictations into a self-updating memory for your AI tools. It keeps context current automatically, so AI answers reflect what is true today.

apps.name: Contextli
apps.tagline: Speak your way through work.
apps.description:
Contextli is a macOS application that functions as a context-aware voice dictation tool. It turns your speech into text formatted for the app you are using, such as a Slack message, an email or a bug report, and pastes it automatically. This tool is designed for professionals, founders, and teams who want to write faster without switching to a separate AI chat.

Key Features:

- Converts speech to text with a single Option-Space hotkey.

- Formats dictation automatically for Slack, email, bug reports and meeting notes.

- Works in any app you can type in, from Gmail and Notion to VS Code and Jira.

- Saves dictations as a searchable feed that AI tools like Claude and ChatGPT can read.

- Available on macOS, Windows, Linux and mobile.

Contextli is a macOS voice dictation app that formats your speech for whichever app you are typing in. It turns quick spoken notes into polished messages, emails and reports, and pastes them automatically.

apps.name: MakerNotch
apps.tagline: Your projects, at a glance, in the notch.
apps.description:
MakerNotch is a macOS application that shows the status of your software projects in the Mac's notch. It brings CI/CD, deployments, infrastructure, revenue and issues from multiple tools into one panel, without switching accounts. This tool is designed for indie makers, founders, and developers who manage several projects and services at once.

Key Features:

- Shows a single health verdict per project, such as all clear or CI failing.

- Connects to 11 tools including GitHub, GitLab, Vercel, Cloudflare Pages, Stripe, Polar, Sentry and Linear.

- Displays deployments, payments, errors, email deliverability and assigned issues.

- Includes a focus timer, notes, bookmarks and music controls.

- Stores read-only API keys in the macOS Keychain and works with or without a notch.

MakerNotch is a macOS application that puts CI/CD, deployments, revenue and issues for all your projects into the notch. It connects to tools like GitHub, Vercel and Stripe so you can check everything without switching accounts.

apps.name: Kiiwi
apps.tagline: Your keystrokes deserve a soundtrack.
apps.description:
Kiiwi is a macOS application that makes your Mac keyboard sound like a mechanical one. It plays real switch recordings from the menu bar with near-zero latency, so typing feels more satisfying on headphones or speakers. This tool is designed for writers, developers, and students who type for hours and enjoy the sound of a mechanical keyboard.

Key Features:

- Offers 38 real mechanical switch recordings across linear, tactile and clicky families.

- Places each key's sound spatially based on its position on the keyboard.

- Plays sounds with near-zero latency and randomised pitch for a natural feel.

- Runs from the menu bar with no window or Dock icon and 0% CPU between keystrokes.

- Detects key presses without reading what you type.

Kiiwi is a macOS menu bar app that makes your keyboard sound mechanical using 38 real switch recordings. It adds spatial, low-latency key sounds for a more satisfying typing experience, without reading what you type.

apps.name: Clippio
apps.tagline: Never lose what you copy on your Mac.
apps.description:
Clippio is a macOS application that functions as a lightweight, native clipboard manager. It saves unlimited copy history, offers fast fuzzy search and on-device OCR, and opens from anywhere with Option-Space, all fully offline. This tool is designed for developers, writers, and professionals who copy and paste constantly and need to find past clips quickly.

Key Features:

- Saves unlimited clipboard history, searchable in milliseconds.

- Extracts text from screenshots and images with on-device OCR.

- Supports sequential multi-paste and direct slot pasting with Option-Command-1 to 9.

- Expands text snippets from short triggers and creates QR codes from links or notes.

- Pauses capture for sensitive data and lets you pin, tag and filter clips.

Clippio is a native macOS clipboard manager that saves your copy history, searches it instantly and extracts text from images offline. It adds snippets, multi-paste and keyboard-first shortcuts to speed up everyday copy and paste.

apps.name: ThoughtDrop
apps.tagline: A little more curious.
apps.description:
ThoughtDrop is a macOS application that delivers short ideas from books in a quiet menu-bar and notch reader. It offers concise insights on topics like habits, focus, creativity and money, with context and author attribution, so you can learn between tasks. This tool is designed for curious readers, students, and professionals who want small doses of learning without another feed.

Key Features:

- Delivers book ideas in the notch or menu bar on your own schedule.

- Covers topics such as habits, focus, design, money, creativity and careers.

- Includes context and book and author attribution for each idea.

- Lets you save or love ideas into collections to revisit.

- Offers a searchable library and topic selection with Pro.

ThoughtDrop is a macOS application that shows short, attributed ideas from books in your menu bar and notch. It helps you learn in small moments between tasks, with options to save ideas and explore their context.

apps.name: NotchOwl
apps.tagline: Keep your day a notch closer.
apps.description:
NotchOwl is a macOS application that puts tasks, focus timers, quick notes and calendar events in the Mac's notch. It keeps a lightweight daily planner one hover or Option-N away, with all data stored on your Mac. This tool is designed for students, makers, and professionals who want to plan and focus without digging through windows.

Key Features:

- Manages tasks and calendar events directly from the notch.

- Runs Pomodoro countdowns and a stopwatch that stay visible while you work.

- Includes a daily notepad that saves as you type and turns lines into tasks.

- Shows insights on completed tasks, focus time and daily activity.

- Opens with a hover or Option-N, and works on displays without a notch.

NotchOwl is a macOS application that brings tasks, focus timers, notes and calendar events into your Mac's notch. It keeps your daily plan one hover away, with all data stored locally.

apps.name: NotchPop
apps.tagline: A dynamic island for your Mac.
apps.description:
NotchPop is a macOS application that turns the MacBook notch into a Dynamic Island. It brings media controls, a file shelf, clipboard history, focus timers, calendar and live business metrics into the bar at the top of the screen, and works on Macs without a notch too. This tool is designed for founders, developers, and productivity-focused Mac users who want quick access to everyday tools.

Key Features:

- Shows now playing controls for Spotify, Apple Music and browser tabs.

- Provides a drop shelf for files and a searchable clipboard history.

- Runs Pomodoro timers, countdowns and hydration reminders.

- Displays revenue from Stripe, Polar and Dodo, plus live visitors from Google Analytics.

- Includes over 20 extensions, such as calendar, weather, local dev servers and AI usage stats.

NotchPop is a macOS application that turns the notch into a Dynamic Island for music, files, clipboard, calendar, focus timers and revenue stats. It keeps everyday tools one click away at the top of your screen, with or without a notch.

apps.name: Maccelerate
apps.tagline: Your Mac. Your Pace!
apps.description:
Maccelerate is a macOS application that makes switching Spaces, Cmd-Tab, Mission Control and App Exposé feel faster. It replaces slow system transitions with speeds and shortcuts you control, while keeping SIP enabled. This tool is designed for developers, multitaskers, and power users who switch between workspaces constantly and want less waiting.

Key Features:

- Speeds up switching between up to ten Spaces with custom shortcuts.

- Accelerates Cmd-Tab transitions to apps on other Spaces.

- Opens Mission Control and App Exposé faster via shortcuts or gestures.

- Offers three speed levels: Fast, Faster and Instant.

- Optionally replaces trackpad swipes with faster Space switching, with SIP left on.

Maccelerate is a macOS application that speeds up Space switching, Cmd-Tab, Mission Control and App Exposé transitions. It lets you choose your speed and shortcuts while keeping system protections enabled.

apps.name: ScreenToast
apps.tagline: Turn your Mac screen recording into a product demo. Automatically.
apps.description:
ScreenToast is a macOS application that functions as a screen recorder for product demos. It automatically adds zooms on your clicks, smooths the cursor, frames your camera and drafts narration, so recordings look edited without manual keyframing. This tool is designed for founders, video editors, and product marketers who need polished demo videos quickly.

Key Features:

- Adds automatic zooms on clicks and smooths cursor movement.

- Records display, window or area in six aspect ratios, including 9:16 and 1:1.

- Frames your camera for each platform, including stacked layouts for vertical video.

- Writes and voices a narration script based on what you did on screen.

- Exports in 4K or ProRes, with everything processed locally on your Mac.

ScreenToast is a macOS screen recorder that turns raw recordings into polished product demos with automatic zooms, smooth cursor movement and camera framing. It can draft narration and export in wide, vertical or square formats, all processed locally.

apps.name: Bytesweep
apps.tagline: Your Mac, explained.
apps.description:
Bytesweep is a macOS application that functions as a disk analyzer, cleaner and system monitor. It shows where disk space went, explains what each item is before you remove it, and cleans safely with a 7-day undo, all on-device. This tool is designed for Mac users, developers, and power users who want to reclaim storage and understand what their Mac is doing.

Key Features:

- Analyzes storage with a treemap and finds duplicates and reclaimable junk.

- Cleans caches, logs, temp files and developer data like Xcode, Docker and npm with a 7-day undo.

- Classifies items as safe to clear, review first, or keep, with plain-language explanations.

- Tracks app updates, login items, wake events and live CPU, memory and network usage.

- Adds a notch panel with live system tiles, a file shelf, clipboard history and screen time.

Bytesweep is a macOS application that shows where your disk space went and cleans it safely with a 7-day undo. It also monitors system health, app updates and background activity, with a notch panel for live stats.

apps.name: Better Shot
apps.tagline: Capture clearly. Share beautifully.
apps.description:
Better Shot is a macOS application that functions as a free, open-source screenshot and screen recording tool. It combines screenshot capture and annotation, screen and camera recording, and a full video editor in one native Swift app, with no account, subscription or watermark. This tool is designed for creators, developers, and teams who make walkthroughs, tutorials and polished screenshots and want an alternative to CleanShot X and Loom.

Key Features:

- Captures screenshots of a display, window or area, with arrows, text, shapes, numbered markers and blur.

- Records the screen with camera, microphone, cursor auto-zoom and five cursor styles.

- Includes a native video editor for trimming, splitting, zooms, backgrounds and MP4/MOV export without a watermark.

- Generates on-device captions and offers OCR and a colour picker.

- Supports 75 customizable shortcuts, a URL scheme for Raycast and Shortcuts, and optional share links via your own R2 bucket.

Better Shot is a free, open-source macOS application for capturing and annotating screenshots and recording polished screen videos. It includes cursor auto-zoom, face cam, on-device captions and a built-in video editor, replacing tools like CleanShot X and Loom in one native app.

apps.name: Orbl
apps.tagline: Your Mac desktop, beautifully alive.
apps.description:
Orbl is a macOS application that turns your desktop wallpaper into a calm, living dashboard. It displays the time, weather, reminders, your Mac's vitals and live business metrics directly on the wallpaper, so the information is there whenever you glance at your screen. This tool is designed for founders, developers, and productivity-minded Mac users who want useful information at a glance without cluttering the menu bar.

Key Features:

- Shows clock, weather, air quality, reminders, countdowns and month/year progress on your wallpaper.

- Displays Mac vitals such as battery, CPU, memory, uptime and connected device batteries.

- Connects to Stripe, Lemon Squeezy, Gumroad, GitHub, Product Hunt and other services via read-only keys.

- Pulls values from any API by pasting a cURL command.

- Includes customizable colour themes and animated desktop pets.

Orbl is a macOS application that turns your wallpaper into a live dashboard showing time, weather, your Mac's vitals and business metrics. It connects to tools like Stripe and GitHub so key numbers stay visible at a glance, without adding menu bar clutter.

apps.name: Locus
apps.tagline: Your quiet place to think
apps.description:
Locus is a macOS application that functions as a private, block-based notes app. It offers blocks, backlinks, nested pages and templates in a native Swift app, with every note stored locally on your Mac instead of a cloud server. This tool is designed for writers, students, and professionals who want a Notion-style workspace without giving up privacy.

Key Features:

- Supports block-based writing with headings, to-dos, toggles, callouts, tables and code blocks.

- Links pages with @ mentions and backlinks, and supports nested pages and workspaces.

- Includes quick capture from the menu bar, daily notes, smart dates and templates.

- Imports from Notion, Obsidian and Apple Notes, and exports to Markdown, HTML or PDF.

- Keeps all notes on your Mac, with Touch ID app lock and version history.

Locus is a macOS application that provides a calm, block-based notes workspace with backlinks, nested pages and templates. All notes stay on your Mac with no account or cloud, making it a private alternative to tools like Notion.

apps.name: Tucket
apps.tagline: Everything you copy, tucked away.
apps.description:
Tucket is a macOS application that functions as a clipboard manager accessible from the MacBook notch. It automatically sorts everything you copy by type, makes text inside screenshots searchable, and keeps all data on your Mac. This tool is designed for designers, researchers, and professionals who collect lots of links, images and snippets and need to find them again quickly.

Key Features:

- Auto-sorts copied items by type with no folders or setup required.

- Reads text inside copied images so screenshots are searchable.

- Groups related clips into boards and turns copied images into moodboards.

- Removes image backgrounds in one click and blocks passwords and keys from being saved.

- Pastes any of the last ten clips with ⌘⌃1–0, with four built-in skins.

Tucket is a macOS clipboard manager that opens from the notch and automatically sorts everything you copy by type. It makes screenshot text searchable and keeps all data on-device, with extras like boards, background removal and quick-paste shortcuts.

apps.name: Pastily
apps.tagline: Your clipboard, but better.
apps.description:
Pastily is a macOS application that functions as a fast, private clipboard manager. It keeps a searchable history of everything you copy, including text, links, code, colours and images, and works completely offline. This tool is designed for developers, designers, and professionals who copy and paste constantly and want to stop losing important clips.

Key Features:

- Saves a searchable history of text, links, code, colours and images.

- Turns hex codes into live colour swatches and saves copied images to disk in one click.

- Auto-expires sensitive clips like passwords and API keys on a timer.

- Offers a paste queue and Notch Island, a live clipboard view in the MacBook notch.

- Runs fully offline with no cloud or telemetry, and is also available on Windows and Linux.

Pastily is a macOS application that keeps a searchable, offline history of everything you copy, from text and code to colours and images. It adds a paste queue, auto-expiring sensitive clips and a notch-based clipboard view to speed up everyday copy-paste work.

apps.name: Stoic
apps.tagline: Your Dolby Vision videos. Without the purple and green.
apps.description:
Stoic is a macOS application that functions as a native HDR video player for Apple silicon Macs. It plays Dolby Vision, HDR10+, HDR10 and MKV files with display-aware colour, brightness and frame timing, using far less CPU than common alternatives. This tool is designed for movie enthusiasts, video editors, and colourists who want HDR footage to look the way it was mastered.

Key Features:

- Plays Dolby Vision, HDR10+, HDR10 and HLG with accurate, display-aware colour.

- Supports MKV, MP4, MOV, WebM, M2TS, MXF, AV1, DTS-HD and ASS subtitles.

- Lets you save moments with timestamped notes, set A–B loops, and export clips.

- Saves HDR stills as HEIC, and locks private folders behind Touch ID.

- Runs natively on Apple silicon with Metal, with no account or telemetry.

Stoic is a macOS application that plays HDR and Dolby Vision videos with accurate, display-aware colour on Apple silicon Macs. It supports a wide range of formats and adds tools like saved moments, A–B loops and HDR stills, all in a lightweight, private native player.

apps.name: DiskMate
apps.tagline: Mac storage full? Get your space back.
apps.description:
DiskMate is a macOS application that functions as a disk space analyzer and cleaner. It shows what is taking up storage, separates files that are safe to clear from ones worth reviewing, and moves anything removed to the Trash so nothing disappears by surprise. This tool is designed for Mac users, developers, and creators who keep running out of storage and want a safe, private way to reclaim space.

Key Features:

- Scans home folders, any folder, or external drives and shows what is using space.

- Sorts results into "Safe to clear" caches and "Worth a look" personal files.

- Includes seven tools: Overview, Search, Space, Cleanup, Duplicates, Apps and Old files.

- Finds duplicates, app leftovers, old downloads, and developer caches like node_modules and Xcode data.

- Works fully offline with no account, moving cleaned items to the Trash instead of deleting them.

categories.name: Design
paragraphs: Most design happens inside one big app, but the work around it doesn't. Reference piles up, exports scatter across folders, and a surprising share of the day goes to finding a file you already made. The apps in this category cover that surrounding work on macOS.
Each one is here because it does a specific job well, not because it has the longest feature list. Open any app for its pricing, a full description, and a link straight to the developer's own site.
tips: File format support — check it handles what you actually ship, from Figma and Sketch exports to PSD, SVG and RAW, without a conversion step in between.
Offline search — an asset library is only useful if you can find things in it without waiting on a sync to finish.
Annotation speed — screenshot tools vary enormously in how fast you can arrow, blur and label something before sending it.
Licensing — one-time licences are still common in this category, so check before you commit to another subscription.

categories.name: Developer Tools
paragraphs: A Mac development setup is mostly small tools that each remove one daily annoyance: exposing localhost to a webhook, seeing what is really eating the CPU, getting back the snippet you copied an hour ago. This category collects the ones worth the install.
Everything listed runs natively on macOS, Apple Silicon included, and links straight to the developer's own site.
tips: Native or Electron — native apps launch faster and cost far less battery, which matters for anything that sits in the menu bar all day.
Apple Silicon builds — look for a universal or arm64 binary rather than something running under Rosetta.
Data handling — for AI clients and clipboard managers, check whether history stays on device and whether you can bring your own API key.
Pricing model — several tools here are one-time purchases and a few are open source, so a subscription is worth questioning.

categories.name: Music & Audio
paragraphs: This is the smallest category on the site, and deliberately so. Audio software on the Mac tends to be either a full DAW or a single-purpose tool, and it is usually the single-purpose ones that people are missing.
Expect editors, converters and small utilities that change how your Mac sounds from one day to the next, rather than another recording suite you would have to learn.
tips: Codec coverage — check for the formats sitting on your drive, not just MP3 and WAV.
Latency — anything processing live audio should be upfront about the buffer size it works at.
Batch handling — converting one file is easy; converting four hundred is where these tools separate.
Permissions — capturing system audio on current macOS versions needs explicit access, so prefer apps that explain what they are asking for and why.

categories.name: Productivity
paragraphs: Productivity is the widest category here, so it is worth reading by what each app replaces: a notebook, a meeting you half-remember, a to-do list you kept losing, or the habit of working four hours without once looking away from the screen.
None of these are systems you have to adopt wholesale. Most are small, live in the menu bar, and stay out of the way until the moment you need them.
tips: Where the data lives — notes and transcripts are personal, so check for local storage or your own iCloud rather than someone else's server.
Export — if you cannot get your text out as Markdown or plain files, changing your mind later gets expensive.
Weight — an app you want running all day should be measured in tens of megabytes, not hundreds.
Subscription or one-time — this category has plenty of both, and the one-time options are often the better deal over a few years.

categories.name: Utilities
paragraphs: Utilities are the apps you install once and then forget you installed, right up until you use a Mac without them. Screenshot tools, disk cleaners, recorders, media players and menu bar oddities all live here.
It is the largest category on the site, largely because the versions built into macOS are usually fine but rarely great.
tips: Overlap with macOS — Screenshot, QuickTime and Storage Management already do a version of most of this, so the question is whether the app is meaningfully faster.
Idle cost — a utility that sits in the menu bar should be close to invisible in Activity Monitor.
Permissions — screen recording and full disk access are powerful, so prefer notarized apps that explain each prompt.
Recent updates — check something shipped in the last year, because abandoned utilities tend to break with every macOS release.

posts.title: The Best Logseq Alternative for Networked Notes (2026)
posts.excerpt: Anytype is the Logseq alternative for people who want local-first, linked notes with end-to-end encryption and object-based structure — typed objects with relations, synced peer-to-peer.

toc.label: Why people look for a Logseq alternative

posts.html:
Anytype is a Logseq alternative for people who want local-first, linked notes with end-to-end encryption and object-based structure. It organizes knowledge as typed objects with relations and syncs peer-to-peer.

Logseq is useful if you want an open-source outliner built on markdown files with a graph view. Anytype is built for people who want structure and encryption beyond an outliner.

Why people look for a Logseq alternative

Logseq is a great outliner, but some people want structured objects, built-in encryption, and a different organization model. You may be looking for a Logseq alternative if you want:

  • Object-based organization, not only outlines
  • End-to-end encryption by default
  • Typed relations between notes
  • Built-in peer-to-peer sync
  • A polished, structured interface
  • Local-first storage with encryption

On-device vs. cloud transcription (and why it matters)
Best real-time transcription apps for Mac

posts.html:
Search “real-time transcription Mac apps” and almost every result quietly cheats: it mixes up apps that transcribe a finished audio file with apps that transcribe live, as you speak. Those are different jobs. This guide separates them, tells you which tools run on-device (so your audio never leaves your Mac), and gives you a straight answer on accuracy and price — including the free option built into macOS that most listicles forget to mention.

Real-time vs. file transcription: the distinction nobody explains

“Real-time” (or streaming) transcription means text appears while audio is still happening — live captions in a meeting, dictation into any text field, or subtitles on a call. File (or batch) transcription means you hand the app a recording and it returns text a moment later. Many “best transcription app” roundups list file-only tools as if they were live. If you need words on screen *during* a conversation, that difference is everything.

💡 Quick rule

Need text while you talk → real-time/streaming tool. Need a transcript after a recording → file/batch tool. Some apps do both — those are the ones worth paying for.

The free option most lists skip: macOS Live Captions

Apple ships Live Captions and Dictation in macOS. Live Captions transcribes any audio playing through your Mac — FaceTime, a podcast, even the room around you — entirely on-device, for free. Dictation turns speech into text in any app with a keyboard shortcut. They aren't the most accurate or feature-rich tools here, but they cost nothing, respect your privacy, and are worth trying before you pay. Competitor roundups almost never mention them because there's no affiliate payout — but you should know it exists.

On-device vs. cloud transcription (and why it matters)

This is the single most important decision and most articles gloss over it. On-device apps run the speech model locally using Apple Silicon — your audio never touches a server, which matters for legal calls, medical notes, journalism and anything under NDA. Cloud apps stream audio to a remote service, which can mean higher accuracy and nicer summaries, but your recordings live on someone else's infrastructure. Pick based on what's in the audio, not just the feature list.
